_comment: Per-credential-type issuance policy: consent, face verification, enablement.
NOT in catalog/, deliberately. The catalogue is issuance-side truth about what a
credential IS — fixed by a rulebook, changing when ISO or the Commission changes it.
Whether THIS deployment demands consent before minting one is the operator's
decision. One artefact answering to two authorities is how four divergent catalogue
copies happened once already.
A consent prompt that does not say what is being consented to is worse than none: it
collects the click without informing the decision. So the PROMPT IS THE POLICY — a
type with no written prompt requires no consent, rather than getting generic wording
that names the credential and nothing it does.
This file is the single source. packages/shared/src/issuance-policy.ts and
vc-core IssuancePolicies both answer to it, and conformance/test-issuance-policy.mjs
fails if either drifts.
`disabled` names configuration ids this deployment will not issue at all (403
issuance_disabled). It is written by PUT /admin/policies/{id} on the Java issuer;
absent or empty means everything the catalogue offers is enabled.
Off by default: medicare-sd-jwt and bank-account-sd-jwt. Each needs an authorised data
source and a legal basis before a deployment issues it (a Medicare number is a restricted
government identifier; a bank account touches CDR and AML/CTF). Checked on BOTH issuance
routes: an admin offer and a wallet's authorization-code request.

consent_prompts.bank-account-sd-jwt: You consent to IDPartners issuing a Bank Account Ownership credential that binds your verified account details to this wallet.
consent_prompts.passport-sd-jwt: You consent to issuing an ePassport credential from your scanned passport data and to the face-verification check.
